Mbed-TLS/mbedtls at rubric 1.0.0, both arms, n=3, one model, one sitting — committed under
`acceptance/targets/mbedtls/1.0.0/`:

  * On "does this codebase use locking, show where and how": answering from the index used
    36% FEWER tokens and 6 turns against 9-12, at the same completeness (7.67 vs 8.00 of 9,
    inside the run-to-run noise), and needed NO source reads at all.
  * On "the same struct member has two names — which, why, who gets which": the index arm cost
    14% MORE and scored the same, because it fell back to grep 8-9 times per run. The index
    answered and its answer did not carry what that question needs.

So: reach for the index first, and expect it to win on structural questions about a symbol and
its neighbours. It is not yet a general win, and a question about how one NAME is spelled
differently for different consumers is a case where it currently is not. Reading source after
the index has named the file is the intended fallback, not a failure.

5	 *

10	 *   entropic mcp-bridge [--project-dir DIR]

18	 * adds entropic to their .mcp.json with `command: "entropic"` and
19	 * `args: ["mcp-bridge"]`, and the engine becomes available as MCP
20	 * tools without writing any code.
21	 *

17	## Library Decomposition
18	
19	The engine is a set of shared libraries with explicit dependency boundaries
20	and explicit interface contracts. Each library has a single responsibility.
21	Arrows in the dependency graph point down only — no circular dependencies.
22	
23	```
24	                    ┌─────────────────┐
25	                    │  librentropic   │  Facade — unified C API
26	                    │     (.so)       │  (entropic.h)
27	                    └───────┬─────────┘
28	                            │ links all
29	       ┌──────────┬─────────┼──────────┬──────────┐
30	       ▼          ▼         ▼          ▼          ▼
31	 ┌──────────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌───────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌────────┐
32	 │inference │ │ mcp  │ │ core  │ │config│ │storage │
33	 │  (.so)   │ │(.so) │ │ (.so) │ │(.so) │ │ (.so)  │
34	 └────┬─────┘ └──┬───┘ └───┬───┘ └──┬───┘ └───┬────┘
35	      │          │         │        │         │
36	      │          │    ┌────┴────┐   │         │
37	      │          │    │  types  │   │         │
38	      │          │    │  (.so)  │   │         │
39	      │          │    └─────────┘   │         │
40	      ▼          ▼                  ▼         ▼
41	 llama.cpp  nlohmann/json        ryml      sqlite3
42	            cpp-httplib                    spdlog
43	```

45	### librentropic-types.so
46	
47	Pure types with zero logic. The universal dependency that every other
48	library links against. Established in v1.8.0.
49	
50	- Message, ToolCall, Directive, GenerationResult
51	- Config structs (ModelConfig, TierConfig, etc.)
52	- Enums (ModelState, AgentState, DirectiveType)
53	- Error types (`entropic_error_t`, `entropic_last_error()`,
54	  `entropic_error_callback_t`)

56	#### Message C Representation
57	
58	Messages are JSON strings at `.so` boundaries, C++ structs internally.
59	The JSON wire format:
60	
61	```json
62	{"role": "user", "content": "...", "metadata": {"source": "user"}, "tool_calls": []}
63	```
64	
65	Within a single `.so`, messages use the C++ `Message` struct. Cross-boundary
66	APIs accept and return `const char* messages_json` (JSON array of message
67	objects). Metadata is an arbitrary JSON object — no fixed schema enforced
68	at the type level.

135	
136	## Interface Contracts
137	
138	Each `.so` boundary is governed by an explicit interface header in
139	`include/entropic/interfaces/`. These are **pure C** at the plugin boundary.
140	C++ interfaces are used ONLY within a single compilation unit / library.
141	
142	### The Rule
143	
144	**All cross-`.so` communication uses C types only.** No `std::string`,
145	`std::vector`, `std::optional`, or C++ vtables cross a shared library
146	boundary. Factory functions return opaque handles. Method calls go through
147	the C API or through C function pointers.
148	
149	This prevents ABI incompatibility between different compilers, standard
150	library versions, or C++ standard revisions.
151	
152	### Contract Headers
153	
154	```
155	include/entropic/
156	├── interfaces/                        Contract headers (.so API surface)
157	│   ├── i_inference_backend.h          Pure C factory + handle interface
158	│   ├── i_mcp_server.h                 Pure C factory + handle interface
159	│   ├── i_storage_backend.h            Pure C factory + handle interface
160	│   ├── i_config_loader.h              Pure C factory + handle interface
161	│   ├── i_hook_handler.h               C function pointer callback types
162	│   └── i_inference_callbacks.h        Function pointer typedefs (core→inference)
163	├── types/                             Shared types (librentropic-types.so)
164	│   ├── message.h                     Messages + metadata
165	│   ├── tool_call.h                   Tool call + result types
166	│   ├── directive.h                   Directive types + wire format
167	│   ├── generation_result.h           Generation output + metrics
168	│   ├── error.h                       Error enum + callback types
169	│   ├── config.h                      Config structs (ModelConfig, TierConfig, etc.)
170	│   ├── engine_types.h                LoopConfig, LoopContext, AgentState, Metrics
171	│   ├── generation.h                  GenerationParams, ResourceProfile
172	│   ├── identity.h                    IdentityConfig, PhaseConfig
173	│   ├── hooks.h                       Hook point enum, callback types
174	│   ├── audit.h                       AuditEntry, AuditLogConfig (v1.9.5)
175	│   └── validation.h                  CritiqueResult, Violation (v1.9.8)
176	├── core/                              Engine internals (librentropic-core.so)
177	├── inference/                         Backend impl (inference .so internal)
178	├── mcp/                               MCP impl (mcp .so internal)
179	└── entropic.h                         Public C API facade
180	```
181	
182	### Plugin ABI Versioning
183	
184	Every plugin `.so` must export an API version function:
185	
186	```c
187	extern "C" int entropic_plugin_api_version();
188	```
189	
190	The loader checks this before calling the factory. If the version doesn't
191	match the engine's expected version, the plugin is rejected with a clear
192	error message. New interface capabilities are added via new version numbers,
193	not by modifying existing interfaces.
194	
195	### Symbol Visibility
196	
197	All `.so` files use explicit symbol visibility. Only factory functions
198	and the C API are exported. Everything else is hidden.
199	
200	```cpp
201	#if defined(_WIN32)
202	  #define ENTROPIC_EXPORT __declspec(dllexport)
203	#else
204	  #define ENTROPIC_EXPORT __attribute__((visibility("default")))
205	#endif
206	```
207	
208	Applied only to:
209	- Factory functions (`entropic_create_server`, `entropic_create_inference_backend`)
210	- C API functions in `entropic.h`
211	- `entropic_plugin_api_version()`
212	
213	### No Third-Party Headers in Interfaces
214	
215	Interface headers must not include third-party library headers. The `json`
216	type from nlohmann/json, `YAML::Node` from ryml, etc. are implementation
217	details that do not appear in any header under `interfaces/` or `types/`.
218	
219	Cross-boundary data uses C types: `const char*`, `size_t`, opaque handles.
220

312	## Error Handling Contract
313	
314	Exceptions must NOT cross `.so` boundaries. All cross-boundary error
315	reporting uses one of:
316	
317	1. **Return codes** — C API functions return `entropic_error_t` enum.
318	2. **Error callbacks** — consumer registers a callback for async errors.
319	3. **Error state on handles** — `entropic_last_error(handle)` returns
320	   the last error message string.
321	
322	```c
323	typedef enum {
324	    ENTROPIC_OK = 0,
325	    ENTROPIC_ERROR_INVALID_CONFIG,
326	    ENTROPIC_ERROR_MODEL_NOT_FOUND,
327	    ENTROPIC_ERROR_LOAD_FAILED,
328	    ENTROPIC_ERROR_GENERATE_FAILED,
329	    ENTROPIC_ERROR_TOOL_NOT_FOUND,
330	    ENTROPIC_ERROR_PERMISSION_DENIED,
331	    ENTROPIC_ERROR_PLUGIN_VERSION_MISMATCH,
332	} entropic_error_t;
333	
334	/// @brief Get the last error message for a handle.
335	/// @return Null-terminated string. Owned by the handle, valid until next call.
336	const char* entropic_last_error(entropic_handle_t handle);
337	
338	/// @brief Error callback type for async error reporting.
339	typedef void (*entropic_error_callback_t)(
340	    entropic_error_t code,
341	    const char* message,
342	    void* user_data);
343	```
344	
345	Within a single `.so`, C++ exceptions are used normally. They are caught
346	at the `.so` boundary and converted to error codes/callbacks.

534	## Compile-Time Configuration
535	
536	Feature selection at compile time via CMake options. All options are
537	abstracted through a generated `entropic_config.h` so the configuration
538	frontend can be swapped (CMake presets today, Kconfig or menuconfig later)
539	without changing any source code.
540	
541	### Configuration Flow
542	
543	```
544	CMakeLists.txt                    Reads CMake options
545	    │
546	    ▼
547	entropic_config.h.in              Template with @CONFIG_*@ placeholders
548	    │
549	    ▼
550	entropic_config.h (generated)     #define CONFIG_ENTROPIC_* values
551	    │
552	    ▼
553	Source code                       #ifdef CONFIG_ENTROPIC_* guards
554	```
555	
556	Source code ONLY reads `#define` from `entropic_config.h`. It never checks
557	CMake variables directly. This makes the configuration frontend-agnostic.
558	
559	### CMake Options
560	
561	```cmake
562	# Build type
563	option(ENTROPIC_SHARED       "Build shared libraries (.so)"          ON)
564	option(ENTROPIC_STATIC       "Build static library (.a)"             OFF)

661	### Three-Layer Architecture
662	
663	Every subsystem follows: interface (C contract) → concrete base (80% logic)
664	→ implementation (20% specifics).

666	```
667	C interface (i_inference_backend.h)     Opaque handle + C functions
668	  └─ InferenceBackend (backend.h)       80% logic: lifecycle, locking, metrics
669	       └─ LlamaCppBackend               20% override: load, generate, stream
670	
671	C interface (i_mcp_server.h)            Opaque handle + C functions
672	  └─ MCPServer (server_base.h)          80% logic: dispatch, permissions
673	       └─ FilesystemServer              20% override: tool handlers
674	
675	ChatAdapter (adapter_base.h)            80% logic: prompt assembly, think-blocks
676	  └─ Qwen35Adapter                      20% override: tool parsing, tags
677	```

679	The C interface is the `.so` boundary. The C++ classes are internal to
680	each `.so` — they never appear in public headers or cross library boundaries.

684	## Config Schema Pattern
685	
686	Structs with defaults + separate validation functions.

688

868	## Handle Lifecycle
869	
870	`entropic_handle_t` is an opaque pointer to the engine's root state object.
871	It owns all subsystems and controls their creation/destruction order.
872	
873	**Creation order** (in `entropic_create` + `entropic_configure`):
874	1. Types/logging (spdlog init, error state)
875	2. Config loader (parse YAML, validate)
876	3. Inference backend (model load deferred until first generate)
877	4. MCP server manager + built-in servers
878	5. Engine core (AgentEngine, ResponseGenerator, ContextManager, DirectiveProcessor)
879	6. Storage backend (optional — NULL if not configured)
880	7. Hook registry (empty until hooks registered)
881	
882	**Destruction order** (in `entropic_destroy`, reverse of creation):
883	7 → 1. Each subsystem's destroy is null-safe.
884	
885	**Optional subsystems:**
886	- Storage (`IStorageBackend*`) — engine works without it (in-memory only)
887	- External MCP servers — engine works with built-in servers only
888	- Hooks — engine works with empty registry
889	
890	**Mandatory subsystems:**
891	- Config (must parse successfully)
892	- Inference backend (must have at least one loadable model)
893	- Core engine (state machine, response generator)

897	## Design Rules
898	
899	1. **Arrows point down.** No circular dependencies between libraries.
900	2. **Pure C at `.so` boundaries.** Opaque handles, C function pointers, C types only. No C++ types cross library boundaries.
901	3. **Plugin ABI versioning.** Every plugin exports `entropic_plugin_api_version()`. Version mismatch = rejected.
902	4. **Three-layer hierarchy.** C interface (contract) → concrete base (80% logic) → implementation (20% specifics).
903	5. **Exceptions do not cross boundaries.** Caught at `.so` edge, converted to error codes/callbacks.
904	6. **No third-party headers in interfaces.** nlohmann/json, ryml, etc. are implementation details.
905	7. **Symbol visibility.** Only `ENTROPIC_EXPORT` symbols are public. Everything else hidden.
906	8. **Permissions ship with tools.** Default-deny from day one. Per-identity granularity added later.
907	9. **Streaming is first-class.** `generate_streaming()` in core interface, raw function pointer callback.
908	10. **Atomic state, mutex transitions.** State queries are lock-free. Only state changes take locks.
909	11. **Cancel token on generate.** Consumer can abort mid-generation via atomic flag.
910	12. **Config via generated header.** `entropic_config.h` generated from CMake, source never reads CMake vars directly. Configuration frontend is swappable.
911	13. **Static build supported.** `ENTROPIC_STATIC=ON` produces `.a` with compile-time plugin registry.
912	14. **Data files are shared.** Same identity prompts, tool JSONs, grammars as Python.
913	15. **Auto-generated Python wrapper.** C API header → Python bindings, no manual sync.
914	16. **Directive wire format.** MCP server `execute()` returns JSON with `{"result": "...", "directives": [...]}` envelope. Directives are typed JSON objects dispatched by the engine's DirectiveProcessor.
915	17. **Bundled data discovery.** Compile-time `ENTROPIC_DATA_DIR`, overridable at runtime via config. Used for prompts, tool schemas, grammars, model registry.
916	18. **Messages are JSON at boundaries.** `const char* messages_json` at C API, C++ structs internally. Metadata is arbitrary JSON.
917	19. **WARM→ACTIVE reloads the model.** llama.cpp ties GPU layer offloading to `llama_model_load_from_file()`, not context creation. WARM→ACTIVE frees the CPU-only model and reloads with `n_gpu_layers` from config. mlock ensures pages stay resident, so the reload is fast (~1-3s PCIe transfer, no disk I/O). This matches the Python `_swap_model()` behavior. (v1.8.2)
918	20. **`log` variable renamed to `logger`.** All inference `.cpp` files use `logger` for the spdlog instance to avoid ambiguity with `entropic::log` namespace and `::log` from `<cmath>`. (v1.8.2)
919	21. **`extract_directives()` lives in MCP, not core.** Core has zero dependency on nlohmann/json. Directive extraction from tool result JSON (parsing `_directives` key) is performed by the MCP layer (v1.8.5), which passes typed `Directive` structs to core's `DirectiveProcessor`. Core never touches JSON. (v1.8.4)
920	22. **Core .so uses default symbol visibility.** `librentropic-core.so` is an internal library, not a plugin boundary. All symbols are visible (`CXX_VISIBILITY_PRESET=default`) so test executables can link directly. Plugin `.so` files retain hidden visibility with explicit `ENTROPIC_EXPORT`. (v1.8.4)
921	23. **`TierResolutionInterface` for cross-.so tier queries.** Core needs tier identity data (auto_chain target, explicit_completion, system prompt) but cannot depend on prompts.so or inference.so. The facade injects a `TierResolutionInterface` (C++ function pointer struct in engine_types.h) — same pattern as `ToolExecutionInterface`. (v1.8.6)
922	24. **Pending delegation stored as typed structs, not metadata strings.** `PendingDelegation` and `PendingPipeline` are optional fields on `LoopContext`, avoiding JSON serialization in core.so. The metadata map remains for genuinely string-keyed data. (v1.8.6)
923	25. **DelegationManager uses callback indirection.** Takes `RunChildLoopFn` and `SwapDirFn` callbacks instead of direct `AgentEngine` references. This avoids circular header dependencies and lets the facade control the wiring. The engine exposes `run_loop(LoopContext&)` as the public entry point for child loops. (v1.8.6)
924	26. **PermissionPersister uses string-based YAML editing, not ryml.** ryml's static library (`libryml.a`) compiles with hidden symbol visibility. When linked PRIVATE into `librentropic-storage.so`, the ryml symbols are stripped, causing unresolved references at test link time. Since PermissionPersister only appends items to a YAML sequence (trivial operation), string-based line editing avoids the dependency entirely. ryml remains the project's YAML parser for config loading in `librentropic-config.so`. ## What entropic is

Entropic is a C++ agentic-LLM engine: a shared-library core (`librentropic.so`) that runs a local LLM (via a bundled `llama.cpp` submodule) as a stateful, tool-using agent loop, exposed through a pure-C API (`entropic.h`) and a CLI binary. It supports MCP tool servers (built-in and pluggable `.so` files), YAML-driven configuration/identities, SQLite-backed conversation storage, and speculative/MTP decoding on top of llama.cpp. `docs/architecture-cpp.md:1-21` is the project's own reference architecture and is authoritative — 48 numbered "Design Rules" entries there record real decisions with version/gh# provenance, not aspirational design.

## Where execution begins

There are two real entry points, not one:

1. **CLI binary** — `src/cli/main.cpp:111` (`int main(int argc, char* argv[])`). It's a thin dispatcher over a table of subcommands (`src/cli/main.cpp:93-97`, `anonymous_namespace{main.cpp}::Subcommand`, `src/cli/main.cpp:77-80`): `mcp-bridge` (`run_mcp_bridge`), `version`, `download`. Per the file's own doc comment (`src/cli/main.cpp:1-23`), `mcp-bridge` is the primary integration point — a consumer adds `entropic` to `.mcp.json` and the CLI relays JSON-RPC/stdio to an already-running engine's unix socket. **The CLI itself never creates an engine or loads a model** — that's Design Rule #36 (`docs/architecture-cpp.md:934`), confirmed by reading `main.cpp`: no call to `entropic_create` anywhere in it.
2. **The engine lifecycle, for whoever hosts it** (a TUI, a consumer app, the `examples/` programs) starts at `entropic_create` — `src/facade/entropic.cpp:241-266`. It allocates the opaque `entropic_engine` handle and does only Phase-0 init (logging, atomic log-id); subsystems stay null until `entropic_configure` — `src/facade/entropic.cpp:1749-1759` — parses the YAML/JSON config and builds them. The documented creation order (`docs/architecture-cpp.md:873-880`) is: types/logging → config loader → inference backend (model load deferred) → MCP server manager → core engine (`AgentEngine` + `ResponseGenerator` + `ContextManager` + `DirectiveProcessor`) → storage (optional) → hook registry. Destruction is the mirror order in `entropic_destroy`.

`AgentEngine::AgentEngine` — `src/core/engine.cpp:135-152` — is where the actual agent-loop object gets built: it wires `ContextManager`, `ResponseGenerator`, and `CompactionManager` together and registers directive handlers.

## Major subsystems (from the library decomposition, `docs/architecture-cpp.md:17-133`)

| `.so` | Responsibility | Key files seen in index |
|---|---|---|
| `librentropic-types` | Pure types, zero logic; universal dependency | `src/types/*` |
| `librentropic-core` | Engine loop, state machine, context mgmt, delegation, directives — **zero deps** on inference/mcp/storage/config | `src/core/engine.cpp` (29 symbols), `compactor_registry.cpp`, `identity_manager.cpp`, `constitutional_validator.cpp` |
| `librentropic-inference-{cuda,vulkan,cpu}` | llama.cpp-backed backend, adapters, sampler, speculative/MTP decode | `src/inference/llama_cpp_backend.{cpp,h}` (78+134 symbols — the largest single unit), `src/inference/orchestrator.cpp`, `adapters/` |
| `librentropic-mcp` + `-mcp-{filesystem,bash,git,diagnostics,web,entropic}` | Tool server base, registry, executor, permission manager, transport (stdio/SSE), per-server plugins | `src/mcp/server_base.cpp`, `tool_executor.cpp`, `permission_manager.cpp`, `servers/*.cpp` |
| `librentropic-config` | YAML config/schema validation, identity/constitution loading, bundled model registry | `src/config/loader.cpp` (40 symbols — largest config file) |
| `librentropic-storage` | SQLite conversation persistence, session logs, audit log | `src/storage/database.cpp`, `backend.cpp`, `audit_logger.cpp` |
| `librentropic` (facade) | Thin layer linking everything; the public C API | `src/facade/entropic.cpp` (149 symbols — by far the largest file in the repo) |

Every `.so` boundary is a **pure-C interface** (`include/entropic/interfaces/i_*.h`) — no `std::string`/vectors/vtables cross a library edge (Design Rule #2, `docs/architecture-cpp.md:900`). Internally each subsystem follows a three-layer pattern: C interface → concrete base with ~80% of the logic → thin implementation override (`docs/architecture-cpp.md:661-677`), e.g. `InferenceBackend` (base) → `LlamaCppBackend` (impl).

## Concurrency (from the lock/thread inventory, not narrative)

The index's thread search found 21 spawn sites total, but only **4 are first-party** (17 belong to the vendored `extern/llama.cpp`): `ExternalBridge::accept_loop` (`src/facade/external_bridge.cpp:796`), `HealthMonitor::monitor_loop` (`src/mcp/health_monitor.cpp:92`), `StdioTransport::stderr_reader_loop` (`src/mcp/transport_stdio.cpp:164`), `SSETransport::sse_reader_loop` (`src/mcp/transport_sse.cpp:107`). The lock inventory shows 97 distinct lock identities, 45 first-party — heaviest first-party users are `AdapterManager` (`src/inference/adapter_manager.cpp`, 11 acquisitions), `MCPAuthorizationManager` (`src/mcp/mcp_authorization.cpp`, 10), `AgentEngine::queue_mutex_` (`src/core/engine.cpp`, 5 acquisitions). Design Rule #10 ("atomic state, mutex transitions", `docs/architecture-cpp.md:908`) matches what's in `InferenceBackend`: `transition_mutex_` guards only lifecycle transitions, state reads are lock-free atomics.

## If you had to change something tomorrow

- **Adding/changing an MCP tool server**: `src/mcp/servers/*.cpp` + the plugin ABI in `include/entropic/interfaces/i_mcp_server.h` (`docs/architecture-cpp.md:222-291` walks the exact contract, including the two required exports).
- **Touching generation/inference behavior**: `src/inference/llama_cpp_backend.cpp` is the single biggest, most load-bearing file (78 symbols, 134 in its header) — read Design Rules #32-46 (`docs/architecture-cpp.md:930-946`) first; speculative/MTP decoding has had multiple hard-won correctness fixes (recurrent-model gating, GQA/flash-attn aborts, lossless-at-any-temperature proof) that are easy to silently regress.
- **Config/identity changes**: `src/config/loader.cpp` (40 symbols) is the biggest src/config file; config resolution order is documented (`docs/architecture-cpp.md:694-698`: compiled defaults → global → project → env vars).
- **CLI/bridge changes**: `src/cli/main.cpp` is intentionally minimal — do not add engine/model logic there (Design Rule #36 is an explicit "forbidden by design").

## Coverage of this answer

- The index holds **2,132 files** total; of those, **`extern/` (llama.cpp submodule) accounts for 1,237 indexed + 49,705 files marked external** — i.e. the vast majority of the physical tree is vendored inference code this answer treats as a dependency, not a subsystem to describe in depth.
- This-repository's own code is small by comparison: `src/` 112 files (1,105 symbols), `include/` 89 files (1,678 symbols), `tests/` 218 files (1,565 symbols), `examples/` 24, `python/` 11.
